findings.address_as_written: Allyne Property, Lots 2 and 3, Assessor's Block 544
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission asked for a $380,000 warrant to complete the condemnation of the Allyne property, Lots 2 and 3 of Block 544, from the estates of Lucy H. Allyne and Edith W. Allyne. At the California Heritage Council's request it had agreed two weeks earlier not to authorize demolition of the house for 90 days, while saying this did not change its plan for a park.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, March 25, 1965, Resolution No. 6170

findings.description: The California Heritage Council asked again to keep the Allyne house as a historical display. Burton Rockwell of the Art Commission said the local chapter of the American Institute of Architects endorsed saving it, and that the house had come around the Horn in pieces and been put together here. The city attorney advised that a museum would be a lawful recreational use, but the federal open-space grant of $114,000 had been approved on the understanding that the house would come down. The Recreation and Park Commission, two members dissenting, voted to go ahead with its original plan for a passive park.
